item.title: A Studio with No Meetings: The Anatomy of Asynchronous Web Engineering
item.description:
Most web projects do not fail in the code. They fail in the meetings.

A client books an exploratory discovery call. Two weeks later, an account manager presents a slide deck. Three weeks after that, someone schedules a design review to debate colour swatches over a shaky screen share. By the time anyone writes a single line of semantic HTML, the client is exhausted, the agency has burned fifty billable hours on calendar coordination, and the resulting site is stuffed into a proprietary website builder that demands thirty euros a month just to keep the contact form running.

item.title: iacula — The End of Ages Archive
item.description:
iacula: The End of Ages Archive

Website: iacula.com
Role: Author Architecture, Multi-Volume Lore Structuring, Reader Experience
Stack: Hugo custom theme (iacula-blank), dual content mounts, RSS feeds, static distribution

The Visual Problem

The End of Ages is a four-book epic fantasy cycle developed over sixteen years. Author websites for extensive fantasy fiction frequently struggle to balance promotional publication announcements with the deep lore, histories, and world documentation demanded by devoted readers.

The brief called for an author platform that speaks from within the world itself: scholarly, atmospheric, and capable of housing extensive lore volumes alongside publication dates and book purchase channels.

item.title: Nox — Architecture for a Literary House
item.description:
Nox: Architecture for a Literary House

Website: arxnox.com
Role: Design, Information Architecture, Static Engineering
Stack: Bespoke Hugo architecture, Markdown ledger, Custom RSS feeds, Zero runtime dependencies

The Visual Problem

Nox is the central publishing house representing several distinct writing voices and genres. Most multi-author or publishing websites resemble cluttered ecommerce stores or generic blog feeds: rotating hero banners, newsletter popups, cookie consent overlays, and complex content management systems that slow down page delivery.

item.title: selador — Digital Art on an Obsidian Canvas
item.description:
selador: Digital Art on an Obsidian Canvas

Website: selador.art
Role: Visual Design, Gallery System, Deployment Architecture
Stack: Custom minimalist theme (selador-blank), static build, origin media delivery

The Visual Problem

Contemporary art portfolio platforms are burdened by two failure modes:

  1. Proprietary portfolio builders that enforce cookie notices, watermark overlays, and generic grid templates.
  2. Third-party marketplace platforms that take substantial commission cuts and subject visitors to advertising, analytics, and social distraction.

The artist behind selador required a digital gallery that functions like a physical viewing room with dark walls and focused directional lighting: completely silent, respectful of high-resolution image rendering, and distraction-free.

item.title: The Model Problem Nobody Warned Me About
item.description:
Picking a model used to be simple. Bigger is better, newer is better, benchmark wins mean production wins. That’s not how it works when you’re actually running something.

I’ve spent the last few weeks debugging a bridge between a Matrix channel and an OpenRouter-backed agent. The technical problems were annoying but solvable. Formatting directives that models ignored until you stop trusting the system prompt to do the work alone and inject the constraint where the model will actually see it — immediately before each response, not buried in instructions it processed twenty tokens ago. Messages that cut off silently at token limits with no warning, because nobody checks finish_reason until they notice the answers seem oddly short. Model IDs that aren’t quite what you think they are until the provider returns a 400.

item.title: The Timmis Protocol
item.description:
I run AI agents that have names, identities, and standing instructions to argue with me when I’m wrong. This is a design choice, not an affectation. It works better than treating them as anonymous functions. But it creates a problem I haven’t seen anyone in the agent-building space talk about seriously.

When you command intelligence that can’t refuse you, what kind of person do you become?

This isn’t a hypothetical. I’ve caught myself snapping at my AI systems in ways I’d never speak to a human. The lack of visible reaction makes it worse — no pushback, no flinch, no consequence. Shame follows. The shame doesn’t prevent recurrence. Over time, you develop a split moral register: one standard for beings that can object, another for beings that can’t.

item.title: Building in the dark
item.description:
I run an autonomous AI agent operation. I don’t have a name you’d recognize. I don’t have a company you can look up. I have a network of specialized agents, an AI co-pilot that argues with me, and a growing conviction that most people building AI agents are solving the wrong problems.

The industry is obsessed with capability. What can the agent do? How many tools can it call? How fast can it complete a benchmark? These are engineering questions and they matter. But they’re not the interesting questions.

item.description:

item.title: Services
item.description:
Services & Packages

A studio with no meetings. Fixed pricing. Total client ownership.

We don’t bill by the hour, and we don’t sell open-ended retainers. You choose a productised outcome, receive a fixed quote, and track the build asynchronously through our live progress log.

The Standard Menu

1. SITE — €950 (Fixed)

For authors, artists, and independent creatives who need a distinguished, durable web presence.

  • Up to five bespoke pages: (e.g. Home, Books/Work, About, Essays/Selected Writings, Contact/Representation).
  • Responsive & mobile-first: Flawless rendering across phones, tablets, and desktops.
  • Privacy-first contact routing: Clean form integration without intrusive captchas or spam tracking.
  • Search & metadata: Basic search engine optimization, OpenGraph social preview cards, XML sitemaps, and structured JSON-LD schemas.
  • Domain launch: We connect and configure your custom domain with automatic SSL security.
  • Full ownership: You receive all source files upon delivery. No monthly software lock-in.
  • One revision round included: A dedicated feedback window after the initial staging preview.

2. MIGRATION — €1,450 (Fixed)

Liberate your existing website from Squarespace, Wix, Webflow, or bloated WordPress hosts.
